block.name: Run a single read-only model fallback for entry points that static discovery missed

scores.evidence: Clean seams. `check_head_citation` and `Break` are made public and shared by the gate and the fallback. `encode_answer`, `TraceContext.answer` and `_trace_request` remove the trace-only coupling. fallback.py is one cohesive module: key, encode, run, `_Filter`, helpers. It defines `log` and starts with `from __future__ import annotations`. No model call happens in the gate or in discovery. Possible smells: entries.py:143 adds a `"model" if entry.kind == "model" else OUTPUT_KIND[...]` special case instead of one kind map. prompts.py `paths_fallback` and fallback.py import each other, which is resolved only by a deferred import inside the function body (possible Inappropriate Intimacy). `UNPLACED = Location(path="(unplaced)")` puts a fake path into a field the contract describes as "A line in a file under the snapshot root".

395 lines of behavioural tests cover the call (one call, read-only, labelled, schema), the prompt (location order, "already listed", citation and untrusted rules, scope), parsing (unknown kind becomes `other`, three malformed shapes, empty answer), each unverified-citation form, three duplicate sources, the same line in another file, collapsing two entries on one line, first-failure order, the accounting invariant, cache reruns, and order-independent bytes. Gaps: the same-handler duplicate branch (`_Filter._duplicate`, second branch) is never exercised, because the `handler-line` case cites the `def` line, which `_taken` already rejects. `test_every_answer_form_gives_the_same_document` never compares documents across forms. The unscoped prompt text ("whole snapshot") is not asserted.

All Block 7 scenarios are implemented: one call after discovery with `paths:fallback` and read-only tools; prompt and key contents; three answer forms; lenient kind; `failed`, `ok` and `skipped` statuses; recoverable vs propagated errors; the three-step filter in order with the right stage and reason literals; kept entries of kind `model` at the cited line, with the enclosing handler, sorted by location; multi-repo paths kept as written. The capability rule "resolves to the same handler as such an entry" is also implemented (fallback.py:168-170). Reachability and coverage for fallback survivors are deferred to block 8, as the spec says. Minor divergences: the handler can be a `class`, and drops with no in-root citation are recorded at a placeholder `(unplaced):1` location the spec does not define (the implementer flagged this).

Produced interfaces match tasks.md exactly: `PATHS_FALLBACK_PROMPT_VERSION`, `paths_fallback(*, commit, scope, entries)`, `FallbackEntry`, `FallbackAnswer`, and `run_fallback(*, ctx, entries, scope) -> tuple[FallbackStatus, list[Entry], list[PathDrop]]`. Kept entries go through the unchanged `trace_entries`/`trace_key`/gate path. Their handler anchors gate rule 6, and `KIND_RANK['model']=9` orders them last. Widening `Entry.kind` to `EntryKind | ModelKind` is safe: the only `OUTPUT_KIND[e.kind]` lookup outside `to_path_entry` is the discovery merge at entries.py:1181, which model entries never reach. Loose seams: `fallback_key` keys only `[kind, path, line]`, while the prompt also shows each entry's name and handler. Two fallback entries at different lines inside one function both get traced, even though path-tracing says entries resolving to the same handler share one trace request.

I have the context I need. Next I'll make the fallback handler pick the enclosing function only, then add the missing tests.Now the tests.Checking that the new class-body test fails against the old `enclosing_def` behaviour:Now checking that the handler-duplicate test fails when that branch is removed:Both new tests fail when the fix is reverted, so they guard real behaviour. Next I'll take `specs/config.yaml` out of the diff and run the full suite.I fixed all four findings. The full suite passes (521 tests) with both the pipeline's test command and the project's own command.

**What changed**
- **Handler is now the enclosing function, not a class** (spec verdict and the Note finding). I added `PyIndex.enclosing_function` in `pyindex.py`. It returns the innermost function `def` around a line and skips classes. `_enclosing_handler` in `fallback.py` now uses it, and the module docstring says so. A line in a class body outside any method now gets no handler, and a line inside a method gets the method. I added a small `Jobs` class to the `pkg/hidden.py` fixture and two cases to `test_handler_is_the_enclosing_def_only_for_python_lines_inside_one`. That test fails if I switch back to `enclosing_def`.
- **The handler-based duplicate check is now tested.** The new test `test_line_inside_a_deterministic_entry_handler_is_a_duplicate` cites `return step1_opal(args)`, a body line of `cmd_opal`. That line is not any entry's location, edge `from` line or handler line, so only the handler check can drop it. The test checks that the drop message names `cmd_opal`, and it fails if I disable that branch.
- **The answer-form test now does what its name says.** `test_every_answer_form_gives_the_same_document` is no longer parametrized. It runs all three answer forms (model, dict, JSON string), writes each result with `write_paths_file`, and asserts the three files are byte-identical. It also keeps the status and path-kind checks.
- **`specs/config.yaml` is out of the block's diff.** I ran `git rm --cached`, so the removal is staged and the file is still on disk for the pipeline.

**One thing to watch:** if the pipeline commits with something like `git add -A`, `specs/config.yaml` will be committed again. I did not add a git exclude rule, because this worktree shares its `info/exclude` file with the main checkout.
